findings.title: Cache is not rechecked after acquiring the write lock
findings.body: GetWebAssets releases the read lock before acquiring the write lock, but never rechecks entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring it. Every goroutine that observed a nil cache during a cold start will therefore serialize on the write lock and repeat the manifest file read and parsing, overwriting the cache each time, while the exclusive lock also blocks fast-path readers for the duration of that I/O. On a burst of concurrent index requests at startup this defeats the cache for that burst and unnecessarily serializes disk I/O; recheck the cache inside the write lock (respecting Dev mode) and return the already-loaded value when another goroutine populated it.

findings.title: No concurrent regression test exercises the claimed race fix
findings.body: This change adds mutex synchronization around entryPointAssetsCache but adds no test that calls GetWebAssets from multiple goroutines. Sequential tests would not have triggered the original data race under the race detector, so removing or misplacing one of the new lock operations in the future would not be caught. Add a same-package test that resets the global cache, serves a valid assets-manifest fixture via cfg.StaticRootPath, hammers GetWebAssets concurrently in non-Dev mode, and is run with -race.
